name: Haemoptysis (oncology context)
description: Haemoptysis is the coughing up of blood or blood-stained mucus from the respiratory tract. In an oncology context, it is a red flag symptom for lung cancer, particularly in patients over 40 with a smoking history. Any new haemoptysis in a patient without a known benign cause (e.g., bronchiectasis exacerbation) warrants urgent chest imaging and bronchoscopy. It may also occur in pulmonary metastases from other primary tumours. Even a single episode of frank haemoptysis without prior respiratory disease requires investigation.
